ai.description: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* is a small skink reaching 45 mm SVL. It is dark brown with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and prominent reddish-orange spots along its flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark reddish-brown lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the flank.
ai.habitat: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* inhabits the leaf litter of moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests within the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* is a diurnal skink that actively forages for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaestlea laterimaculata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the high-elevation montane forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
